rationale: The Old English verb a-teáh (a-tēon, "to draw out/forth") in the cited passages (Cri. 1494, Beo. Th. 1537) carries the sense of something coming forth or issuing out, which aligns best with issue_forth.v.01 ("come forth"). The "a-" prefix (ā-) marks directed motion away or outward, matching the "come forth / issue" sense rather than simple approach (come.v.01) or arrival (arrive.v.01).
